title: Code Intelligence's Spark agent found a heap use-after-free in wolfSSL's pem_read_bio_key() during its beta test; wolfSSL merged a fix within days and shipped it in 5.7.6
summary: Spark, an AI fuzz-test agent, found a heap use-after-free in wolfSSL in late Oct 2024; fixed in PR 8139 and shipped in 5.7.6 on 31 Dec 2024.
account: Spark, the AI test agent in Code Intelligence GmbH's CI Fuzz product, was run on wolfSSL, an open-source cryptography library for embedded and IoT devices, in its final beta test in late October 2024. By the vendor's account, after one command the agent chose the target, generated and ran a fuzz test, and exposed a heap use-after-free in pem_read_bio_key(), where a BIO write-back could reallocate a buffer still referenced by a pointer. The vendor reported it to wolfSSL, which merged a fix in PR 8139 on 1 November 2024 and shipped it in release 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024, crediting 'Peter' in the release notes; the vendor's blog post on the find is by its engineer Peter Samarin.
purpose: Spark was built to find bugs and vulnerabilities autonomously by selecting functions to fuzz and generating and running fuzz tests; finding this flaw was exactly that function, exercised in the vendor's own beta test.
system: Spark, AI test agent in Code Intelligence's CI Fuzz (invoked as 'cifuzz spark')
deployer: Code Intelligence GmbH (beta test run by the vendor)
domain: Software security / open-source cryptography library testing
segment: Open-source TLS and cryptography library for embedded and IoT systems
taxonomy_note: No listed type covers security hardening. Chosen because the agent surfaced a flaw the maintainers did not know about, which is the information they needed to fix it. The vendor's claim that Spark saves up to 1,000 hours of manual effort is marketing about the product, not part of this event.

ratings.reason: wolfSSL received a reproducible report of a heap use-after-free in a private-key parsing path and merged the fix within days (PR 8139, 1 November 2024), shipping it in 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024. The maintainers listed it among bug fixes rather than in the release's Vulnerabilities section, no CVE for it appears on wolfSSL's vulnerabilities page, and the vendor itself says the exploit conditions 'don't seem easy to meet', so the benefit is material but bounded.

ai_role.statement: On the vendor's account, Spark selected the target, generated the fuzz test and ran it after a single 'cifuzz spark' command, with one manual step to confirm that the finding was real and exploitable under narrow conditions. wolfSSL's pull request and release notes confirm the bug, its location in pem_read_bio_key(), the timing and the reporter's first name, but mention neither AI nor Code Intelligence; the autonomous discovery therefore rests on the vendor's statements, repeated by QA Financial and SC Media, not on an independent test.

must_hold: A human must confirm the finding: the vendor says the one manual step was assessing that the bug exists and is exploitable under specific conditions
The beneficiary must be an identifiable project with a public fix record; without wolfSSL's PR and release notes the event would rest on vendor claims alone
The AI's share of the work is described only by the vendor; wolfSSL's records name the reporter, not the tool, so the autonomy claim cannot be replicated without the vendor's product
